svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The timeline of life on Earth (approximate dates)."], [1, "Earth forms 4.6 billion years ago; the first cells appear by about 3.5 billion years ago."], [4, "Cyanobacteria add oxygen to the air from about 2.4 billion years ago."], [6, "Eukaryotes appear about 1.8 billion years ago; multicellular life about 1 billion years ago."], [8.5, "Zoom in on the last 540 million years: animals, plants on land, dinosaurs, mammals, flowering plants."], [13, "As a 24-hour day, humans arrive in the last few seconds."]]
svg.title: The timeline of life
svg.desc: A timeline of Earth's 4.6 billion years with eons and the first cells, oxygen, eukaryotes and multicellular life, a zoom into the last 540 million years, and the history of Earth as a 24-hour clock.
svg.text: The timeline of life on Earth
Dates approximate, in billions of years ago (bya) and millions of years ago (mya).

g.data-info: Hadean (4.6–4.0 bya), Archean (4.0–2.5), Proterozoic (2.5–0.54) and Phanerozoic (0.54 bya to now). bya = billion years ago.
For roughly the first 2 billion years of life, all organisms were prokaryotes.
Photosynthetic cyanobacteria released oxygen; it began to build up in the air about 2.4 billion years ago.
The first eukaryotic cells, about 1.8 billion years ago, probably by endosymbiosis.
Almost all the animals and plants we know appear in the last eighth of Earth's history.
If 4.6 billion years were 24 hours, modern humans would appear about 6 seconds before midnight.

g.text: If Earth's history were one day (from midnight):
